area: Stock / placeholder imagery: where it lives, what renders it, and how to make it unmistakable in dev
summary: Every photograph a customer can see on this site today is Unsplash stock, and nothing in the code or the data says so. I read the live database (read-only GET via PostgREST, service-role key from .env.local, 2026-07-27): all 20 customer-visible salons have a cover_photo_url, all 20 point at images.unsplash.com, and there are only 11 distinct URLs among them, so 13 of the 20 salons are wearing a photo that also belongs to another salon (one image is the cover for four different waxing studios). Their galleries are 166 URLs, also 100% Unsplash. salon_photos has 0 rows. The marker the owner assumed exists does not work: salons.is_test is a real column read as a hide-filter by 15+ API routes, but it is false on all 28 rows, so it flags nothing and currently discriminates nothing. There is no dev-only banner component anywhere in the repo, and no isStock/isSeed helper of any kind. next.config.mjs allowlists exactly three stock hosts (unsplash, pexels, picsum) alongside supabase/tiktok/googleusercontent, so the allowlist itself is a usable definition of "stock". Separately: of the 46 hardcoded Unsplash literals in app/lib code, 28 sit in dead components nobody imports, and one (booking/lookup) is live, ungated, and shipped before the gate that would now block it.

gaps.what: A machine-readable flag on the data that says 'this photo is stock'. Today the ONLY signal is the hostname in the URL string. salons.is_test exists but is false on all 28 rows, so it carries zero information.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every downstream consumer (UI, gates, audits, the design-verifier's imagery floor) has to re-derive 'is this real?' by string-matching a hostname. The moment a real salon uploads to Supabase Storage and a seeded one still points at Unsplash, nothing in the schema distinguishes them and the imagery floor keeps scoring against fake content.
gaps.existing_thing_to_extend: salons.is_test (already a column, already read by 15+ API routes) — or, cheaper and with zero migration, the hostname allowlist already enumerated at next.config.mjs:88-110

gaps.what: Any visual distinction between stock and real imagery in dev/preview. No banner, no ribbon, no filter, no data attribute exists anywhere.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is the owner's literal complaint. Twenty salon cards render four duplicate Unsplash photos and look exactly like a finished product, which is why the same mistake keeps getting re-made across sessions.
gaps.existing_thing_to_extend: app/layout.tsx:59-64 (the single <head>) — no new component needed

gaps.what: An enforcement check that FAILS on stock or duplicated salon covers. The scaffold exists but always passes, and the audit script it delegates to was never written.
gaps.why_it_matters: scripts/check-invariants.mjs already contains the correct diagnosis in prose (lines 302-320) and reports it forever without ever blocking. The duplication it describes is still exactly true today, ten days later.
gaps.existing_thing_to_extend: scripts/check-invariants.mjs checkSalonPhotoIntegrity() at line 302, plus the npm script check:invariants at package.json:15

gaps.what: The 12 p01-p12.jpg files that public/_mockups/_BASE.md:33 makes law. They are not on disk and not in git; only README.txt is tracked.
gaps.why_it_matters: Four mockups silently paint #F4F4F5 grey boxes where the base law promises real photos, and the mockup gates that check for _assets/salon-photos see the reference and pass.

recommendation: Do the CSS-level marker first, because it is the only option with complete coverage and it touches one file.
